section_summary: This section covers diplomatic, military, and legal deliberations regarding cultural property and Japanese art objects between late 1948 and September 1949. Major topics include the unsuccessful Japanese requests for the restitution of culturally valuable swords surrendered during the occupation and dispersed as souvenirs among U.S. servicemen, as well as the resulting press leak and investigation. Additionally, it details U.S. opposition in the Far Eastern Commission to Allied proposals for replacing lost cultural objects from Japan's cultural heritage prior to a formal peace treaty, and concludes with State Department endorsement of a private initiative led by Joseph C. Grew to organize a U.S. exhibition of ancient Japanese art.

subfiles.about: Provides a legal opinion on whether surrendered Japanese swords of artistic value constitute cultural objects wrongfully taken under SWNCC 322.
subfiles.summary: Snow concludes that swords classified as national treasures or important art objects are cultural objects wrongfully taken under SWNCC 322.
subfiles.title: Are Japanese Swords Cultural Objects Wrongfully Taken Within Meaning of SWNCC 322

subfiles.about: Explains refusal to initial a draft instruction because privately owned Japanese swords are being wrongfully kept by occupation authorities.
subfiles.summary: Yingling declines to initial the draft instruction, maintaining that privately owned arms seized during occupation must be restored at peace.
subfiles.title: Draft Instruction to USPOLAD for Japan Regarding Japanese Swords

subfiles.about: Advises against characterizing surrendered civilian swords as legitimate war trophies under the 1907 Hague Regulations.
subfiles.summary: Yingling argues civilian swords were surrendered post-war and cannot be considered war trophies under the 1907 Hague Regulations.
subfiles.title: Restoration to Japanese Individuals of Swords of Artistic Value Turned Over to American Forces

subfiles.about: Contains handwritten drafting notes regarding whether surrendered Japanese swords may be regarded as legitimate trophies of war under international law.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten draft discussing whether surrendered Japanese swords received in good faith can be regarded as legitimate war trophies under international law.
subfiles.title: Draft Note Regarding Japanese Swords as War Trophies

subfiles.about: Conveys the Department of the Army's view that tracing and returning surrendered art swords to Japan is impractical.
subfiles.summary: The Army Department agrees that tracing and returning surrendered swords dispersed among veterans is administratively impractical and expensive.
subfiles.title: Return of Swords Classified as Objects of Art

subfiles.about: Recommends instructing the U.S. representative on the Far Eastern Commission to oppose compulsory replacement of lost cultural objects from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Fearey recommends opposing the FEC replacement program for cultural objects, proposing the issue be deferred to the peace conference.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Cultural Objects

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP CIE's request and Japanese Government documents seeking the return of registered national treasure and art swords.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards a request by SCAP's Civil Information and Education Section for State Department assistance in recovering artistic Japanese swords surrendered in error and taken to the United States. The despatch encloses a detailed Ministry of Education inventory of missing designated swords and an official petition from the Central Liaison and Coordination Office requesting their restitution.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 727: Return to Japan of Swords Classified as Objects of Art

subfiles.about: Circulates an amended proposed policy decision on the replacement of cultural objects lost or destroyed due to Japanese aggression.
subfiles.summary: Circulates an amended policy paper requiring Japan to replace lost Allied cultural objects with equivalent items, excepting certain national treasures.
subfiles.title: SC-272/12: Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects

subfiles.about: Circulates amendments submitted by the Soviet member to the proposed policy on replacement of lost cultural objects.
subfiles.summary: Circulates Soviet amendments to SC-272/12 proposing Japan replace cultural objects in national and public use and deleting paragraph 7a.
subfiles.title: SC-272/13: Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects - Proposed Soviet Amendments

subfiles.about: Informs the Assistant Secretary of the Army that the State Department will instruct its FEC representative to oppose SC-272/12.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth advises Voorhees that the State Department will instruct its FEC representative to oppose SC-272/12 and defer cultural replacement to peace.
subfiles.title: Opposition to FEC Policy on Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects

subfiles.about: Instructs the U.S. representative to oppose SC-272/12 and maintain that replacement of cultural objects should await the peace conference.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes the U.S. member to oppose SC-272/12, stating replacement cannot properly be dealt with during occupation and must await peace.
subfiles.title: Instruction to U.S. Member, FEC: SC-272/12, Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Expresses the Department of the Army's satisfaction with the State Department's instructions to oppose SC-272/12.
subfiles.summary: West acknowledges Butterworth's letter of March 29 and notes the Army's satisfaction with instructions opposing SC-272/12 in the FEC.
subfiles.title: Army Concurrence on U.S. Position Regarding SC-272/12

subfiles.about: Instructs the U.S. FEC representative to oppose SC-272/12 while expressing sympathy for Allied cultural losses.
subfiles.summary: Official instruction authorizing General McCoy to oppose SC-272/12 while conveying sympathy for Allied cultural losses to the commission.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for United States Member, FEC: SC-272/12, Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Informs Tokyo that attempting to locate and return surrendered Japanese art swords is neither expedient nor practical.
subfiles.summary: State Department instructs Tokyo that tracing and returning surrendered swords is impractical and expensive, concurring with the Army.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 68 to USPOLAD Tokyo: Return of Swords Classified as Objects of Art
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Provides a copy of the Army Department letter concluding that recovering surrendered swords from veterans is impractical.
subfiles.summary: File copy of Colonel Porter's letter stating that tracing and recovering Japanese swords from scattered veterans is impractical and futile.
subfiles.title: Army Views on Return of Swords Classified as Objects of Art (Copy)

subfiles.about: Transmits Despatch No. 727 to the Army Department and requests its views on recovering surrendered art swords.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman forwards Despatch No. 727 to Voorhees, suggesting tracing swords is impractical and requesting the Army's views.
subfiles.title: Request for Army Views on Return of Swords Classified as Objects of Art (Copy)

subfiles.about: Provides guidance to the U.S. FEC member in response to Chinese inquiries regarding replacement of cultural property.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth provides a statement for General McCoy responding to Chinese queries, asserting that cultural property replacement requires a peace treaty.
subfiles.title: Statement Regarding Replacement of Japanese Cultural Objects
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Reports a Chicago Daily News press story on the sword decision and orders an immediate investigation into the leak.
subfiles.summary: Acheson cites a Chicago Daily News article reporting the sword decision and orders an immediate investigation of the confidential leak.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Telegram No. 200 to SCAP Tokyo: Leak of Sword Instruction
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports on the investigation of the press leak, noting ties between correspondent Keyes Beech and CIE fine arts officials.
subfiles.summary: Huston reports that Chicago Daily News correspondent Keyes Beech lives part-time with CIE fine arts adviser C. F. Gallagher.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-130: Press Leak Concerning Japanese Swords

subfiles.about: States that the leak investigation was inconclusive and recommends against issuing a corrective public statement.
subfiles.summary: Huston reports the investigation failed to identify the leak's source and concurs with CIE that no corrective statement is needed.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram No. 201: Investigation of Sword Leak

subfiles.about: Contains a brief archival pencil or file notation reading 'selvas OK'.
subfiles.summary: Brief file notation reading 'selvas OK'.
subfiles.title: File Note

subfiles.about: Inquires whether the Department of State objects to Grew chairing a committee organizing a U.S. loan exhibition of ancient Japanese art.
subfiles.summary: Grew asks Butterworth whether the Department objects to his chairing a committee bringing a Japanese painting exhibit to the U.S.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Proposed Japanese Art Exhibit in the United States

subfiles.about: Welcomes the proposed Japanese art exhibit and supports Grew serving as chairman to improve cultural relations.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth endorses the proposed Japanese art exhibition under Grew's leadership as a valuable step toward rebuilding cultural goodwill after the war.
subfiles.title: Response Regarding Proposed Japanese Art Exhibition
